text: dsh-marktext 是面向 DSH Web 侧栏的 MarkText（muya）Markdown 所见即所得编辑器。它注册 .md、.markdown、.mdown 和 .mkd 文件标签，在隔离的 iframe 中显示编辑器，并由宿主提供文件打开、状态读取和保存接口。用户可以直接编辑排版后的文档、查看相对图片、通过版本校验保存，并使用快捷键与自动保存；客户端主题和语言会跟随宿主。适合需要在 DSH 中查看和修改 Markdown 文档的用户。插件不需要 API Key 或额外账号；运行依赖 DSH 的 sidebarRightTabs、slots、fs 与 webServer 服务。

dsh-marktext adds the MarkText (muya) WYSIWYG editor to the DSH Web sidebar. It opens Markdown files in an iframe, supports editing, relative images, and version-checked saves, and follows the host theme and locale. It requires DSH sidebar and file services; no API key is needed.
想在 DSH 侧栏里直接编辑 Markdown 文档。
有没有能把 .md 文件打开成所见即所得编辑器的功能？
让 DSH 打开 Markdown 时显示排版后的页面，而不是纯源码。
我改完文档后，希望保存时能发现磁盘文件已经变化。
在 DSH 里编辑 Markdown 时，怎样让文档旁边的相对图片也显示？
想在侧栏里用快捷键和自动保存编辑 Markdown。
I want to edit Markdown as a rendered document in the DSH sidebar.
Can DSH open .md files in a WYSIWYG editor and save them safely?
dsh-marktext 的功能「侧栏 Markdown 标签」：在 DSH 右侧栏将 .md、.markdown、.mdown、.mkd 文件注册为 marktext 标签，并在 iframe 中打开编辑器。
dsh-marktext 的功能「打开与保存」：读取选中文件的正文和版本信息，再把编辑后的内容保存回文件；保存请求必须带原版本，文件已变化时返回版本冲突。
dsh-marktext 的功能「相对图片加载」：打开文档时为其目录生成短期 token；渲染器请求的相对资源先从插件资源中查找，再从该文档所在目录加载。
dsh-marktext 的功能「Markdown 文件链接」：渲染器发出打开链接消息后，客户端把本地资源地址交给 DSH 侧栏打开为另一个标签；外部链接则交由浏览器打开。
dsh-marktext 的功能「跟随宿主外观」：客户端将主题状态和语言传给 iframe 编辑器，并观察宿主主题变化以更新显示。
dsh-marktext 的功能「注册状态诊断」：插件记录侧栏标签类型与标签内容的注册情况，并通过本地诊断接口报告状态，便于查看标签未显示时的注册结果。
dsh-marktext 使用前须知：渲染 PlantUML 图表时，随附的渲染代码会访问 www.plantuml.com 的 PlantUML 服务；图表内容可能随渲染请求发送。

dsh-marktext README · Introduction：

English · 简体中文

**Click a `.md` in the sidebar and it opens as the finished document** — headings, tables, math, diagrams and images, all editable in place. No split pane, no source-and-preview dance. Save with `⌘S`; the file goes back to disk through a version guard, so you never overwrite someone else's edit.

dsh-marktext README · Introduction：> MarkText is an Electron desktop app. This plugin doesn't ship its shell — it takes the editor core MarkText extracts ([`@muyajs/core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@muyajs/core) / muya, MIT) and adds only the DSH integration. Everything runs locally.

dsh-marktext README · Why it feels different：- **✍️ You edit the document, not the source.** Markdown markers stay hidden; headings, lists, tables and quotes are real elements. Put the caret in a table cell and fix the cell, not a row of pipes.
- **📊 Diagrams and math just render.** KaTeX, Mermaid, Vega and PlantUML ship with the plugin and load on demand — offline, no CDN, no account.
- **🖼️ Images land where you expect.** `` resolves against the document's own folder, so docs written in your editor look right here.
- **💾 Saving is boring, in the best way.** Autosave 2.5 s after you stop typing; `⌘S` saves immediately; a changed file on disk means a conflict banner, never a silent overwrite.
- **🌗 It looks like DSH.** Light and dark follow the host, and the editor never adopts a foreign theme.
- **⌨️ Your fingers already know it.** `⌘Z` / `⇧⌘Z` undo and redo, `⌘S` saves, `⌘F` finds — nothing to relearn.

dsh-marktext README · Install in one line：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-marktext
```

**Using the Desktop app?** Open **Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin**, enter `dsh-marktext`, click **Enable now**, then restart the app once. (The desktop profile is managed by the app, so the CLI line above is for `dsh web` only.)

dsh-marktext README · What you get：| | | |---|---| | **Open any Markdown**
`*.md`, `*.markdown`, `*.mdown`, `*.mkd` in the sidebar open in an editing tab. | **Real editing**
Tables, code blocks, quotes, task lists — direct manipulation, not text surgery. | | **Math & diagrams**

dsh-marktext README · Under the hood：```
DSH Web (React)
  lib/client.js  ── sidebar tab kind `marktext` (patterns: *.md)
      │             tab body = <iframe src="/dsh-marktext/renderer/<token>/index.html">
      │ postMessage (single envelope: __dshmkt)

The editor runs in an iframe on purpose: muya declares its CSS variables on `:root` and appends floating toolbars to `document.body`, so inlining it would leak styles into the host. The iframe isolates all of that; only document, theme and save calls cross the boundary.

dsh-marktext README · Under the hood：<details>
<summary>Message protocol (v1) and the file-policy fallback</summary>

Envelope: `{ __dshmkt: true, dir: 'down' | 'up', type, content }`

dsh-marktext README · Under the hood：| Direction | type | content |
|---|---|---|
| down | `doc` | `{ path, displayPath, text, version, dark, locale }` |
| down | `saved` | `{ version }` |
| down | `save-error` | `{ code, message }` |
| down | `theme` | `{ dark }` |
| up | `ready` | — |
| up | `dirty` | `{ dirty }` |
| up | `save` | `{ text, baseVersion }` |
| up | `reload` | — |
| up | `open-external` | `{ href }` |

dsh-marktext README · Under the hood：**Saving and the file policy.** The normal path is `ctx.fs.writeText(target, text, { kind: 'replaceIfVersion', version })`; a stale version returns `FS_STALE_VERSION` and the UI shows a conflict banner. If the host policy refuses the write (`FS_SANDBOX_DENIED`, e.g. `workspace-write` / `read-only`), the save falls back to Node's `fs.writeFile` **with the version guard intact** — the version is checked before and re-read after. Real OS errors (`EACCES` / `EPERM`) still surface as-is.

</details>

dsh-marktext README · Troubleshooting：If a `.md` opens but the tab says something like "no viewer available", the client half didn't register its tab body. Read the registration report:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<DSH-port>/dsh-marktext/api/diag | python3 -m json.tool
```

`typeRegistered`, `bodyRegistered` and `errors` point at the failing step.

dsh-marktext README · FAQ：**Is this the MarkText app?** No. It's MarkText's editor core (muya) wrapped for DSH — no Electron, no desktop shell, no second app to install.

**Will it reformat my file?** It saves what the editor serializes, which is standard CommonMark/GFM. The version guard is what protects you: if the file changed underneath, you get a conflict, not a silent rewrite.

**Does it work offline?** Yes — every asset, font, diagram engine and syntax highlighter ships with the plugin.

dsh-marktext README · FAQ：**Does it fight with other Markdown plugins?** Both it and `dsh-markdown-typora` claim `*.md` in the `extension` band, so install one of them, not both.

**Known limits:** absolute image paths (`/abs/a.png`, `file://`) aren't resolved yet; no "insert selection into chat"; no PDF export. Package size ≈4 MB tarball; first paint ≈1.6 MB.

dsh-marktext README · Development：```sh
npm install
npm run build:renderer            # writes renderer/ (committed; only needed when src/renderer changes)
npm test                          # host routes, version guard, traversal, origin fence, client registration
node scripts/verify-renderer.mjs  # headless Chrome: open → render → save → disk

dsh-marktext README · Release：Publishing uses **npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)** — no token or secret in the repo. Every push to `main` runs tests, verifies the committed `renderer/` matches `src/renderer/`, publishes only when the version is new, and creates a **GitHub Release** (`v<version>`, generated notes).

```sh
npm version patch --no-git-tag-version
git commit -am "chore: release x.y.z"
git push
```
